hyperedges.label: Deterministic non-LLM Services Extracted from the SAS

nodes.label: Lead-to-Visit WhatsApp Agent — Agentic System Design
nodes.rationale: Designed within ArchitecturalDrivers v0.2 constraints (Chatwoot SoR conversations, wacrm SoR leads, FastAPI+Supabase AI domain, organization-ready modular monolith). ARSDA verdict 4.15 — Scale with Caution: validate PMF via journey KPIs before scaling volume.
nodes.norm_label: lead-to-visit whatsapp agent — agentic system design

nodes.label: Coordinator Agent (SAS)
nodes.rationale: Single LLM agent owns the entire happy-path dialogue because the task is strongly sequential with dependent states (intent→discovery→qualification→matching→objections→visit); MAS would degrade 39-70%. Context 4/5: only current state + profile + last N messages, never full history.

nodes.label: Intent Router
nodes.rationale: Single short LLM call classifying lead intent into 6 categories; low confidence triggers a confirmation question, persistent ambiguity escalates to human. Runs on a small model for cost.

nodes.label: Qualification Flow (Prompt Chaining)
nodes.rationale: Gradual discovery via sub-prompts per profile dimension, each verifiable — reduces compounded error versus one big extraction.

nodes.label: Objection Handler (LLM+RAG)
nodes.rationale: Answers objections only with verified KB evidence or declares it doesn't know — never invents figures; without KB evidence it offers to consult the broker. Kept as a SAS node (depends on conversational context) but with external KB.

nodes.label: Guardrails Layer
nodes.rationale: Last line before irreversible action: hard rules for discounts (register offer, never promise), money/documents (immediate human handoff), prices (only from inventory, never LLM memory), availability (only pre-validated slots). Risk overrides complexity — confirming a visit is conversationally simple but its failure is the critical business risk.

nodes.label: Matching Engine (deterministic + RAG)
nodes.rationale: Extracted as a deterministic non-LLM service (SQL filters + pgvector + Availability Validator) because it is reusable and independent — it will also serve the future seller flow. 0 results emit an explicit 'reframe search' signal, never a silent empty list.

nodes.label: Availability Validator
nodes.rationale: Deterministic validation bottleneck mitigating the critical business risk (booking a visit to an unavailable property, 0 tolerance KPI). 'pending' status blocks client confirmation; automatic re-check 2-4h before the visit. Marked as one of three critical failure points.

nodes.label: Scheduling Service
nodes.rationale: Deterministic service materializing a validated visit in Google Calendar with 24h/2h reminders; API failure retries with backoff and the client is never notified without external confirmation.

nodes.label: Ownership Policy Engine (rules)
nodes.rationale: Rule-based (E14 matrix) because no conversion data exists yet — registered as strategic debt with exit plan: ML optimization over OwnershipDecision+Outcome in Phase 3. Stale wacrm data (>60s) forces re-sync before deciding.

nodes.label: BuyerProfile
nodes.rationale: Persistent memory-managed profile with immutable versioning — the agent never overwrites, it appends versions. Completeness checkpoint before matching cuts propagation of bad profiles.

nodes.label: SAS + Deterministic Services Hybrid Decision
nodes.rationale: SAS chosen over MAS because: task is strongly sequential with dependent states; a single well-tooled agent clears the 45% baseline rule; ~8-10 tools would fragment token budget across agents in MAS; low error tolerance demands a centralized validation bottleneck (contains error amplification to 4.4x vs 17.2x). Reusable independent capabilities are extracted as non-LLM services. Seller flow (A6) routed to a future independent agent — different domain.

nodes.label: Autonomy Matrix (Risk × Complexity)
nodes.rationale: Assigns autonomy level per system decision: greetings/FAQs fully autonomous; discount negotiation and money/documents are human-only hard guardrails; visit confirmation requires deterministic availability validation. Rule: risk dominates complexity.

nodes.label: LangGraph Framework Recommendation
nodes.rationale: LangGraph scored 4.65 weighted (vs Pydantic AI 3.80, ADK 3.85, CrewAI 2.80, Agno 3.30): the Nuevo→Dormant→Reactivated lifecycle demands persistent resumable checkpoints (conversations sleeping weeks) and first-class HITL interrupts for Rules 1-4. Pydantic AI runner-up: its models define tool contracts INSIDE LangGraph nodes (combination, not exclusion). CrewAI discarded: role crews add nothing to a sequential SAS; ADK couples to GCP unnecessarily.

nodes.label: Conversation State Machine (15 CRM states)
nodes.rationale: Nuevo→…→Postventa aligned to the 15 wacrm CRM states plus Dormant (reachable from any active state) and Reactivated→OwnershipEvaluation as sole re-entry. AI operates from Nuevo to VisitaAgendada; from VisitaRealizada onward the owner is human (E14 scenarios 3-4).

nodes.label: Error Compounding Mitigation
nodes.rationale: ~6 chained LLM decisions at 90% each ≈ 53% end-to-end success — unacceptable. Mitigation: highest-risk steps (matching, availability, scheduling) made deterministic and removed from the probabilistic chain; profile completeness checkpoint before matching; explicit lead confirmations (user as free validator). Effective chain ~4 steps at 95% target ≈ 81-85% expected; failures fall to reframe/escalate paths, never to a mis-booked visit.

nodes.label: Eval Pipeline (10 QA cases in CI/CD)
nodes.rationale: The 10 journey QA cases (property reserved mid-chat, long audio, couple from one number, price mismatch, reactivation weeks later, etc.) are the foundational eval set; regression on any QA case blocks deploy. Expanded later with anonymized real transcripts (debt: eval set is only 10 cases until +60 days).
nodes.norm_label: eval pipeline (10 qa cases in ci/cd)

nodes.label: AIDecisionTrace (per-decision tracing)
nodes.rationale: Every decision traces agent/node, prompt version, referenced context, tools with parameters, cost, latency, output and resulting state (Gate 9); stored in Supabase and surfaced in the AI Sidebar for broker explainability.

nodes.label: Typed Tool Contracts (9 tools)
nodes.rationale: 9 typed contracts (get_lead, update_profile, search_properties, check_availability, propose_slots, book_visit, send_property_pack, handoff, register_offer). Key controls: price ALWAYS from the system never conversational context (QA-6); book_visit requires Status=confirmed plus intent validation; register_offer only records, never accepts (Rule 2).

nodes.label: AI Sidebar (Chatwoot)
nodes.rationale: Human review surface: edge-case qualification review, escalation target for guardrails, and explainability window over decision traces.

nodes.label: ARSDA Scorecard (4.15 — Scale with Caution)
nodes.rationale: 10-gate scorecard: build capability now, scale volume only after Gate 1 (PMF validation). Bottlenecks to monitor: PMF validation and wacrm availability. Horizontal/vertical calls: Availability Validator and Matching separated (reusable); ranking/filtering integrated into Matching; Objection Handler integrated as SAS node with external KB.

nodes.label: ArchitecturalDrivers.md v0.2 — AI-Native Real Estate Lead Qualification Platform
nodes.rationale: Living document defining epics E1-E14, quality attribute scenarios QA-01..QA-14, constraints and 8-sprint MVP roadmap. Source of truth for WHAT the system must achieve; Architecture.md describes HOW. v0.2 added Data Ownership, E14 Ownership Policy Engine, and dormancy/reactivation lifecycle.
nodes.norm_label: architecturaldrivers.md v0.2 — ai-native real estate lead qualification platform

nodes.label: Data Ownership (System of Record)
nodes.rationale: Each system is authoritative for exactly one data category; all others hold synchronized replicas. AI domain never mutates lead stage directly — it emits events to wacrm and consumes confirmed state back. Conflicts resolve in favor of the SoR with asynchronous idempotent reconciliation. Principle: 'Chatwoot manages conversations. wacrm owns the lead. FastAPI owns intelligence.'

nodes.label: Chatwoot (SoR: conversations)
nodes.rationale: System of Record for conversations, messages and inbox assignment; constraint: never forked, never replaced.

nodes.label: wacrm (SoR: leads and pipeline)
nodes.rationale: System of Record for leads, pipeline stage, broker assignment history and negotiation status. Its synchronization quality and latency directly condition ownership decisions (QA-13).

nodes.label: Supabase (SoR: AI domain)
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL + pgvector, System of Record for the AI domain: buyer profiles, embeddings, Knowledge Graph, Prompt Registry, tool configuration, decision traces.

nodes.label: Coordinator (AI module)
nodes.rationale: Central AI module orchestrating Qualification, Recommendation, Neighborhood, Calendar, CRM and Follow-up; also implements the broker-request guardrail bypassing policy evaluation for zero-latency transfer.

nodes.label: Ownership Policy Engine (E14)
nodes.rationale: Ownership is never binary AI-vs-Human: 'Re-entry → Context Evaluation → Best Owner'. 10-scenario rule-based decision matrix configurable per organization (never-human→AI; visit occurred→previous broker; negotiation→previous broker always; >12 months→full requalification; explicit broker request→Coordinator guardrail bypass). Platform differentiator; Phase 3 replaces rules with a model trained on per-owner conversion outcomes, instrumented from Sprint 4.

nodes.label: Conversation Lifecycle (dormancy and re-entry)
nodes.rationale: Any active state can decay to Dormant (org-configurable triggers); every reactivation passes through OwnershipEvaluation — never returns to a fixed owner. Humans can take over at any point; ClosedLost leads may re-enter via campaigns. Makes QA-09 verifiable.

nodes.label: Broker-Request Guardrail (Scenario 8)
nodes.rationale: When the customer explicitly asks for a broker ('¿Está María?'), the Coordinator bypasses policy evaluation and transfers immediately. Implemented as a conversational guardrail, not a policy rule, to guarantee zero-latency deterministic transfer.

nodes.label: Continuous Learning Loop
nodes.rationale: Conversations, Meet transcripts and CRM feed Discovery→Extraction→Embeddings→Knowledge Graph→Market Insights, which feed back into Prompt Registry, Recommendation, Buyer Persona, ICP and RAG. Conversion outcomes per owner decision captured from day one so E14 can evolve from rule-based to data-driven.

nodes.label: Recommendation Engine (E4)
nodes.rationale: Top-3 properties via structured filters, RAG and Google Maps. Critical importance, High difficulty — Sprint 3 split into 3A (core) and 3B (neighborhood enrichment) to de-risk the highest-difficulty sprint.

nodes.label: CRM Synchronization (E7)
nodes.rationale: Bidirectional, idempotent lead/stage/activity sync with wacrm. Escalated in v0.2 from 'synchronization' to critical runtime dependency of the Ownership Policy Engine — ownership decisions on stale data (>60s, QA-13) are detected and re-evaluated.

nodes.label: Human Handoff Mechanics (E8)
nodes.rationale: Executes ownership transfer with a full context package (profile, recommendations, conversation summary). Separation of concerns with E14: E14 decides WHO and WHEN; E8 executes the transfer mechanics.

nodes.label: Prompt Registry (versioned, per organization)
nodes.rationale: Minimal versioned registry required from Sprint 0 (architectural concern: prompt versioning); the administration UI arrives only in Sprint 6 (E12) on top of it.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith Constraint
nodes.rationale: Technical constraints: FastAPI owns business logic, PostgreSQL+pgvector on Supabase, event-driven internal architecture with idempotent consumers, single deployment multi-organization with organization_id logical isolation, no Chatwoot fork, small team, MVP first, no SaaS features until PMF. Microservices extraction deferred to Phase 4.

nodes.label: QA-03 Organization-Ready Scalability
nodes.rationale: A new agency onboards through configuration only — no code changes, no redeploy. Logical isolation via organization_id on all business aggregates. Deliberately NOT full multi-tenancy: self-service onboarding, billing and tenant provisioning explicitly out of scope until PMF.

nodes.label: QA-09 Ownership Reliability
nodes.rationale: Conversation ownership always derivable from the state machine: every transition passes through OwnershipEvaluation or an explicit guardrail; no conversation simultaneously AI-owned and human-owned; no reactivation bypasses policy. Verified by state-machine property tests.

nodes.label: QA-13 Data Consistency (60s staleness bound)
nodes.rationale: Pipeline stage, broker assignment and negotiation status in the AI domain must reflect wacrm with max 60s staleness; ownership decisions taken on stale data are detected and re-evaluated.

nodes.label: QA-14 Qualification Quality (completeness gate)
nodes.rationale: ≥90% of leads reaching Recommendation must have a complete buyer profile (budget, location, property type, timeline); incomplete profiles are blocked from recommendation with a targeted follow-up question.

nodes.label: Lead to Sales System — Architecture Document
nodes.rationale: Built via ADD (Attribute-Driven Design) in 9 incremental iterations, each closing goal→elements→concepts→instantiation→decisions→driver coverage. Contains context/container/component/deployment views, 27 sequence diagrams, port contracts, event catalog and Design Decision Records with discarded alternatives. Sized for ~10 agencies / ~9,000 leads/month, scalable x10 without structural redesign.
nodes.norm_label: lead to sales system — architecture document

nodes.label: Coordinator Agent (LangGraph)
nodes.rationale: LangGraph orchestration with persistent checkpoints; new nodes (Qualification Iter.3, Recommendation Iter.4, Appointment Iter.5) added without touching existing nodes (QA-06). Stateless workers with retry/backoff — conversation state lives in Postgres, not process memory, enabling 24/7 availability and horizontal scaling without session affinity.

nodes.label: Conversation State Machine (persisted FSM)
nodes.rationale: Explicit FSM persisted in Postgres with Dormant/Reactivated/OwnershipEvaluation as first-class states — makes QA-09 verifiable by construction: invalid transition raises InvalidTransitionError with no write. Survives restarts (dormancy spans months). Discarded: ad-hoc boolean flags, in-memory FSM.

nodes.label: Guardrail Interceptor
nodes.rationale: Maximum-priority layer executed BEFORE Coordinator reasoning, with direct bypass to the Ownership Policy Engine — zero latency and determinism for '¿Está María?' (scenario 8). Discarded: letting the LLM decide the bypass (non-deterministic, unacceptable for a hard rule). Since Iteration 7 reads its rules from the Guardrail Configuration Service instead of hardcoded Rules 1-4.

nodes.label: Ownership Policy Engine (Decision Table)
nodes.rationale: Grew skeleton (scenarios 1+8, Iter.2) → +scenario 2 (Iter.5) → full 10-scenario Decision Table with PolicyRules ordered by priority (Iter.6), never changing the evaluate(context)->OwnershipDecision signature — QA-06 validated four consecutive times. Unimplemented scenarios returned explicit NotImplementedPlaceholder, never silent defaults. Property-based tests guarantee exactly one rule wins per evaluation. Discarded: if/elif chains, Drools-style full rule engine (over-engineering).

nodes.label: Chatwoot Webhook Adapter (ACL)
nodes.rationale: Anti-Corruption Layer translating Chatwoot events to domain events and back; acks webhooks in <1s while the Coordinator processes asynchronously via the Event Bus (QA-01) — decouples LLM latency from webhook timeout. Future channels (Telegram, QA-04) only touch this adapter.

nodes.label: AI Sidebar Publisher
nodes.rationale: Publishes state, ownership and explanations into Chatwoot for broker consumption — explainability by construction: explanation fields are first-class, not derived logs (QA-11).

nodes.label: Event Bus (Transactional Outbox/Inbox)
nodes.rationale: Outbox+Inbox over the same Postgres: event written in the same transaction as the domain change (no inconsistency window), single-writer worker publishes, consumers deduplicate by event_id (at-least-once, idempotent handlers). Discarded: Kafka/RabbitMQ day 1 (operational overhead unjustified at ~0.07 events/sec), naive dual-write.

nodes.label: Versioned Configuration Store
nodes.rationale: One versioned-table-with-active-flag pattern reused three consecutive times: OrganizationConfig, PromptTemplate/PromptVersion, and OwnershipPolicy — versioning and rollback for free, single point of config resolution avoiding per-module settings sprawl (CRN-9). transcriptSource field reserved from Iteration 1 to avoid a later schema migration.

nodes.label: Row-Level Security by organization_id
nodes.rationale: Entry middleware resolves organizationId and executes SET app.current_org before any module query — isolation enforced by the database engine as defense in depth, impossible to 'forget' the filter. Discarded: schema-per-tenant and database-per-tenant (Phase 4 architecture, violates single-deployment constraint).

nodes.label: Lead Sync Adapter (bidirectional ACL)
nodes.rationale: Sole read/write point to wacrm (RBAC + audit centralized, QA-08). CDC via polling with syncedAt watermark cursor — resumable after any crash, works even if wacrm webhooks are unreliable. Writes to wacrm go through the same Outbox pattern.

nodes.label: Staleness Guard
nodes.rationale: Explicitly invoked before every critical decision; forces synchronous re-sync if isStale() exceeds 60s, blocking the decision until data is fresh — materializes QA-13 as verifiable behavior, not documentation. Discarded: trusting periodic polling alone (a crashed worker breaks QA-13 silently).

nodes.label: Completeness Gate (Specification pattern)
nodes.rationale: External precondition of the Qualification→Recommendation transition (QA-14): completeness < threshold returns false + missing dimension, prompting a targeted question. Kept outside the FSM so the FSM stays generic and the business rule has a single point of truth.

nodes.label: BuyerProfile Capture Service (progressive profiling)
nodes.rationale: Captures the buyer profile one dimension at a time as a LangGraph node (Prompt Chaining) — each sub-question is simple and verifiable, reducing compounded error. Discarded: single capture form (worse conversational UX, higher abandonment).

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval (SQL filters + pgvector)
nodes.rationale: Structured SQL filters (budget/zone/type) discard impossible candidates cheaply, then pgvector semantic search over the filtered subset captures qualitative intent — better precision than either alone. Discarded: pure RAG (could return properties over budget), pure SQL (misses unstructured intent). Embeddings precalculated at ingestion, never generated per search.

nodes.label: Ranking Engine (deterministic, no LLM)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic score = Σ(RankingSignal.weight × value); adding a new signal never changes the signature (QA-10). Discarded: LLM ranking over the property list (non-deterministic, breaks auditability and explainability).

nodes.label: Explanation Generator
nodes.rationale: Receives only the winning RankingSignals; the LLM only phrases them into natural language, never decides content — every explanation is traceable to a real signal, preventing hallucinated reasons (QA-11). The LLM never sees the full property list.

nodes.label: Neighborhood Enrichment Adapter
nodes.rationale: Fan-out/fan-in parallel Google Maps calls over only the final Top-3 (not all candidates — bounds cost/latency); on timeout delivers a partial fallback and completes asynchronously via NeighborhoodEnriched event — latency budget (<15s) prioritized over message completeness.

nodes.label: Availability Validator (deterministic bottleneck)
nodes.rationale: Mandatory validation bottleneck before proposing or confirming any slot, with owner/admin confirmation when no real-time inventory state exists and automatic re-validation 2-4h before the visit. Deterministic and auditable — does not depend on the LLM 'remembering' to check. Never caches beyond a short TTL.

nodes.label: Scheduling Service
nodes.rationale: Materializes a validated visit as an Appointment; requires AvailabilityValidatorPort status=confirmed; internally invokes the Calendar Adapter with conferenceData.createRequest.

nodes.label: Google Calendar Adapter
nodes.rationale: Single port: create_event with conferenceData.createRequest returns event + Meet hangoutLink in one API call — no separate Meet port or adapter exists, reflecting the real mechanism. Discarded: modeling Meet as an independent integration (duplicated architecture over a single call).

nodes.label: Reminder Scheduler
nodes.rationale: 24h/2h reminders persisted as jobs in Postgres, independent of the synchronous booking flow — survives restarts of the process that booked. Same scheduling pattern as decayToDormant() and Follow-up Scheduler.

nodes.label: Handoff Package Builder (Facade)
nodes.rationale: Assembles profile + recommendations + conversation summary exclusively through existing ports (BuyerProfileCapturePort, RecommendationPort, FSM) — never direct table access across modules. The broker never receives a 'blank' conversation.

nodes.label: Outcome Listener
nodes.rationale: Listens to DealClosed/VisitCompleted/ClosedLost and links the real business result — known weeks later — to the original OwnershipDecision, accumulating the Phase 3 ML training signal without future schema change. The Coordinator cannot write the outcome at decision time because it doesn't exist yet.

nodes.label: Reactivation Detector
nodes.rationale: The ONLY component authorized to emit ReactivationEvent; verifies the conversation is Dormant before emitting. Follow-up Scheduler and Campaign Dispatcher never invoke the Ownership Policy Engine directly — no signal generator decides the owner.

nodes.label: ReactivationEvent (domain event)
nodes.rationale: Sole trigger of OwnershipEvaluation; payload includes source (reply | campaign | new_property). Ensures no reactivation path bypasses policy evaluation (QA-09).

nodes.label: Follow-up Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Independent job triggered by Dormant transitions per org-configured thresholds; fires nurturing messages but never assigns an owner.

nodes.label: Campaign Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Batch campaigns to cold leads with per-lead response tracking; never invokes the Ownership Policy Engine directly — replies flow through the Reactivation Detector.

nodes.label: Admin Gateway (versioned CRUD + RBAC)
nodes.rationale: Thin layer over existing Configuration Store ports; versioned CRUD with rollback for prompts, org config and ownership policies. RBAC with 4 roles per organization (owner, admin, broker, viewer), backed by RLS — roles never cross organization_id. Discarded: parallel admin data store, fine-grained per-resource ACLs (over-engineering for a small team).

nodes.label: Tool Registry (passive catalog)
nodes.rationale: Catalogs each ToolDefinition (typed input/output schemas + riskLevel feeding guardrails); validates schemas once at registration, not per invocation — no latency added to the critical path.

nodes.label: Guardrail Configuration Service
nodes.rationale: Turns the journey's 4 hardcoded guardrail rules into per-organization data in the Configuration Store — rule adjustments no longer require a deploy. First documented modification of a prior iteration's component behavior.

nodes.label: Dashboard Query Service (CQRS read)
nodes.rationale: Read-only aggregation over AIDecisionTrace with materialized views (cost per agent, p95 latency, decisions/hour) — trace reads never compete with the critical business write path. Segmentation Dashboard (Iter.8) extends it rather than creating a separate service.

nodes.label: Meet Transcript Adapter (Strategy)
nodes.rationale: Strategy over transcriptSource (agency_workspace | platform_default), reusing the field reserved in OrganizationConfig since Iteration 1 — closes the transcripts driver without schema migration; encapsulates the data-governance difference between agency and platform perimeters; never mixes both modes for one organization.

nodes.label: Conversation Mining Pipeline (batch ETL)
nodes.rationale: Asynchronous batch ETL over the accumulated MessageRef archive + transcripts, outside the conversational critical path; can reprocess the full corpus without affecting production. Real-time per-conversation extraction discarded — insights are aggregates.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Builder (incremental)
nodes.rationale: Consumes existing domain events (MessageReceived/VisitCompleted/DealClosed) to update the graph incrementally instead of full rebuilds that grow costlier as the corpus grows; persists nodes/relations in Postgres+pgvector.

nodes.label: Market Insight Discovery Service
nodes.rationale: Derives Buyer Personas, ICPs and trends from the Knowledge Graph with MANDATORY provenance — no insight is applied automatically to a prompt or ranking signal without a verifiable source and admin approval via the Admin Gateway. Same explainability principle as OwnershipDecision and RecommendationItem.

nodes.label: AIDecisionTrace (aggregate)
nodes.rationale: One record per AI decision: agent, prompt version, tool calls, context refs, cost, latency, output (QA-07 / ARSDA Gate 9). OpenTelemetry instrumented from the FIRST request with generic fields, avoiding costly observability retrofitting; agentName/promptVersionId populate once real agents exist.

nodes.label: OwnershipDecision (auditable record)
nodes.rationale: Persistent record of each policy evaluation: input snapshot, selected owner, human-readable explanation (QA-11) — auditable and replayable. Paired with OwnershipOutcome it becomes the Phase 3 ML training dataset, captured from Sprint 4 with no schema change required.
